page: Amazon Web Services hpc7a.96xlarge is a dedicated compute-intensive instance tailored for tightly coupled high-performance computing, large-scale computational simulations, and parallel processing workloads. Operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the server provides 192 dedicated physical cores across the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9R14 processor architecture running at 3.7 GHz without simultaneous multithreading. Memory provisioning includes 768 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, allocating exactly 4 GB of memory per core. The instance includes advanced instruction set extensions such as AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 support, complementing an extensive per-core cache infrastructure with 32 MB of L3 cache. No local NVMe storage or dedicated graphics processing units are packaged with this server configuration.

Data throughput and interconnect performance reflect its distributed HPC design, offering 300 Gbps of baseline networking bandwidth. In multi-threaded execution benchmarks, the 192-core AMD architecture demonstrates top-tier computational performance, placing within the top decile on stress-ng multi-core tests, PassMark CPU benchmarks, and Clang compilation tasks. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 704.22 GB/sec, and write bandwidth achieves 345.83 GB/sec, providing sustained data delivery to each physical core for high-bandwidth scientific simulations. The architecture shows top-decile capability in prompt processing for language models and memory-heavy operations like Redis execution, while token generation remains constrained by pure CPU limits compared to dedicated accelerators.

From a cost and resource allocation perspective, the server maximizes throughput per socket for compute pipelines that scale linearly with physical core density and memory speed. The omission of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached or remote parallel storage fabrics, which aligns with external HPC cluster architectures. Amazon Web Services hpc7a.96xlarge is best suited for computational fluid dynamics, finite element analysis, weather modeling, molecular dynamics, massive distributed software compilation, and large-scale mathematical batch processing.
description: Amazon Web Services hpc7a.96xlarge is a high-performance computing instance designed for demanding compute-bound parallel workloads. Powered by the Nitro hypervisor and an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor, it offers 192 dedicated physical cores on the x86_64 architecture operating at 3.7 GHz with single-threaded core execution. The system features 768 GB of DDR5 memory at 5 GHz, delivering 4 GB per core alongside AVX-512 vector extensions. Networking throughput reaches 300 Gbps, facilitating rapid node communication across clusters. The instance provides no integrated local storage and contains zero GPUs. Benchmark results place it in the top 10% for multi-threaded CPU stress tests, large-block memory bandwidth, and software compilation throughput. Without local NVMe disks, storage depends on network-attached options. The hpc7a.96xlarge provides a balanced density of memory bandwidth and raw physical compute, making it appropriate for computational fluid dynamics, seismic processing, complex simulations, and scientific research clusters.
